chunks: And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Madaini, from Abu Umayra, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Trimming the nails on Friday saves one from leprosy, leucoderma, and blindness. If it is not possible to trim them, one should at least rub them on something.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of trimming nails on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith links the Friday ritual of grooming to both physical purification and spiritual readiness for worship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition). The specific mention of protection from leprosy (*judham*) and blindness underscores the holistic view of bodily health as a prerequisite for spiritual clarity, while the alternative of rubbing (*hakkaha*) demonstrates the juristic flexibility (*rukhsah*) for those with limited mobility or resources.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Isa from Abi Ayoob’ al-Madaini from Abi ’Umayra from Hisham b. Salim from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Trimming nails on Friday saves one from leprosy, leucoderma and blindness. If it is not possible to trim them, one should at least rub them on something.”
